# @knock-ai/sdk

> The Knock AI SDK for marketing sites and logged-in apps: identify people, track events, and open
> the Knock scheduling modal. npm package: `@knock-ai/sdk` (formerly `knockai`, same API). Zero
> dependencies, core ≤ 1.74 KB gzip, safe to import on the server.

## Install

npm: `npm install @knock-ai/sdk`, then `import { knock } from '@knock-ai/sdk'`.
No build step: paste the CDN snippet from README.md ("CDN (no build step)") into `<head>`, once. It
defines the same API on `window.knock` (and on `window.knockai`, for pages that already use `knock`).

Framework bindings: `@knock-ai/sdk/react`, `@knock-ai/sdk/vue`, `@knock-ai/sdk/angular`. Test mock:
`@knock-ai/sdk/testing`.
With an AI coding agent: `npx skills add knock-org/knock-sdk` installs the install skill for the
agents it detects (`-a <agent>` to choose). Then ask the agent to install the Knock SDK (in Claude
Code, `/install-knock-sdk`; in Codex, `$install-knock-sdk`). An agent without skills support can
follow
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/knock-org/knock-sdk/main/skills/install-knock-sdk/SKILL.md
directly.

## Minimum working integration

```ts
import { knock } from '@knock-ai/sdk';

knock.init({ tagId: 'YOUR_TAG_ID' }); // website tag id on a marketing site; product tag id in a logged-in app

knock.identify({ email: currentUser.email }); // as soon as you know who it is
```

Calls made before the SDK is ready are queued (up to 1,000) and sent in order once it is, so no
readiness check is needed. On the server every call does nothing.

## Two tags

- Marketing site: init with the website tag's id. `identify()` captures a lead; Knock may research
  the lead's company to help the sales team. The tag captures what it is set up to capture (page
  views, clicks, forms).
- Logged-in app: init with the product tag's id. `identify()` tells Knock which signed-in customer
  this is. Nothing is captured by default, only the app's `track()` and `identify()` calls (plus
  clicks on Knock's widget, if shown).
- Same API on both. After ready, `knock.surface` is `'website'` or `'product'` (`undefined` before
  ready, and on older tags).

## API (exact types ship in the package, under `dist/types/`)

- `init({ tagId, debug?, scriptUrl? })`: call once; a second call is ignored. `debug: true` prints
  the SDK's own warnings.
- `identify(traits)`: one argument. `traits.email` is required; `firstName`, `lastName`,
  `company` (a company name string) and other fields are optional. Safe to call more than once.
- `track(name, properties?)`: names are lowercased and turned into snake_case, cut to 64 characters,
  and must start with a letter. Property values: string, number, boolean, Date (sent as an ISO
  string), string[] or null; about 8 KB total. Invalid events are dropped without an error.
- `modal.open({ magicLinkId?, email? })` / `modal.close()`: omit `magicLinkId` for the default
  Knock modal; `email` is only used with `magicLinkId`.
- `scheduling.load({ magicLinkId, email?, onStatusChange? })` returns `{ open(), close(), status }`.
- `widget.show()` / `widget.hide()` / `widget.open()` / `widget.close()`
- `on(event, handler)` returns an unsubscribe function. Events: `ready`, `modal:open`,
  `modal:close`, `widget:open`, `widget:close`, `error`. `ready` fires once; a handler added
  after that still runs, once.
- `wrapLink(url)` returns `url` with the visitor's Knock identity added, so a Knock chat link
  (`start-chat.com`, `login.start-chat.com`) opened from it keeps who the visitor is. Synchronous;
  before the Knock tag is ready and on the server it returns `url` unchanged; never throws. Call it
  when the link is opened (in a click handler, or around a `window.open` URL), not at render.
- Read-only: `knock.ready`, `knock.version`, `knock.surface`.
- React: `KnockProvider`, `KnockButton`, `KnockLink` (a plain `<a>` that calls `wrapLink` when
  the link is opened, never at render), `useKnock`, `useKnockIdentify`, `useKnockEvent`. Vue:
  `KnockPlugin`, `useKnock`, `KnockButton`. Angular: `provideKnock`, and `inject(KNOCK)` for the SDK in components.

## Rules for an AI agent adding this SDK

- Call `init()` once, as early as possible. Use the tag id the user gives you.
- Call `identify()` right after sign-in or session load in an app, or once a visitor gives their
  email on a site. Not on every render.
- Don't use trait names the website tag already sends. These include `userId`, `sessionId`,
  `vendorId`, `tagId`, `tagVersion`, `clientId`, `version`, `uidSource`, `timestamp`, `pageVisit`,
  `pageNumber`, `tabPageNumber`, `revisionNumber`, `referrerUrl`, `utm_source`, `utm_medium`,
  `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`, `utm_term`, `hubspotutk`, `gclid`, `__khsc` and `elementCopy`.
- Don't build magic link ids or event names from user input.
- In Next.js, `KnockProvider` can render from a server component; call the hooks only from client
  components.
- Don't change the CDN snippet's code.
- For a raw link to Knock chat in the code: in React, swap `<a href>` for `<KnockLink href>` with
  the same props; elsewhere, in its `click` and `auxclick` (middle-click) handlers, skip
  `event.button > 1`, set `event.currentTarget.href = knock.wrapLink(url)`, and put `url` back with
  `setTimeout`; wrap a `window.open` URL with `knock.wrapLink()`. Never wrap at render time.

- docs/quickstart.md: install, init options, first identify and track

- docs/frameworks/{react,vue,angular,vanilla}.md
